findings.evidence: tests/conftest.py imports harness.usage during conftest loading, but does not replace _usage.append_jsonl until the session autouse fixture is set up. Test modules are imported during collection before fixture setup, so a module containing `from harness.usage import append_jsonl` captures the original function. Calling that alias without `log_dir` during the test bypasses the patched module attribute and can write to `logs/usage/`. The purpose-written tests only call `usage.append_jsonl` through the module attribute, so they do not exercise this boundary.
findings.required_change: Install the guard before test-module collection so imports receive the guarded callable, while retaining appropriate cleanup, and add a purpose-written test that imports/captures `append_jsonl` in the same way a test module would and proves an unredirected call fails before writing and names the protected directory.
findings.summary: A test can retain and call the original unguarded append_jsonl function.

summary: The suite passes as written, but the guard can be bypassed by a normal import form, allowing a test to write to the real usage directory.
